title: Context + Memory Tradeoffs: Annotated Survey & Personal Cheatsheet
content:
Purpose: quick, skimmable personal reference for tradeoffs when designing long-context LLM features (chat history, doc context, retrieval cache). Not a paper — working notes + experiment ideas + rough cost heuristics.

High-level framing:
- There are three main levers to get long context behavior: model capability (architectural changes, sparse attention), external retrieval (RAG), and runtime memory (KV caches, prefix caching, chunked attention). Each has different cost/latency/accuracy profiles.
- Goal: pick strategies that keep tail latency < 250ms for typical interactive flows while limiting token compute spend to within host budget.

Papers + quick takeaways (one-liners):
- "Efficient Transformers" (survey families: sparse, low-rank, kernelized): generally save compute for extremely long sequences but often require model re-training; brittle when plugged into off-the-shelf checkpoints. Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.06732 — note: implementation risk high.
- "KV-Memory and Retrieval-augmented Models" (several recent arXiv demos): KV caches give low-latency repetition-friendly speedups at inference but increase memory pressure and complicate parallelism. Good for conversational state. Example study: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17580 — useful baseline for cache eviction policies.
- "Chunking & Sliding Window Attention" (practical): easy to retrofit, predictable cost but hurts global coherence if chunk boundaries misalign with discourse.
- "MoE & Routing for Long Context" (emergent): intriguing cost/quality sweet spots but hardware and implementation complexity high.

Observations from recent conference/workshop (MLSys 2027 — session notes):
- Panel consensus: mixed approach wins. Use lightweight retrieval for large corpora, KV caches for conversational recency, and short-term sliding attention for document windows.
- Two production war stories: one company used adaptive chunk sizes based on punctuation boundaries and got ~12% quality gain vs fixed chunking for summarization tasks.

Runtime design considerations (practical):
- Memory cost per cached step: estimate GPU RAM ~ 16 bytes * hidden_dim * seq_len entries for single precision KV; with quantized keys/values this can shrink 2–4x. For 1.5B model (hidden_dim~2048) and 2k tokens cached, raw KV memory ~ 16 * 2048 * 2000 = ~65MB (rough). Always validate with model dtype and implementation details.
- Network cost: cloud-hosted dedicated pools may move KV shards between worker nodes. Sharding strategy matters: colocate KV with compute that will use it most.
- Eviction strategies to try: LRU time-based, salience-weighted (attention mass), and segmented TTL per conversation type.
- Batching implications: larger batches allow better throughput but increase per-request latency; micro-batching + async completion can give steady tail behavior.

Simple cost model (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline token FLOPs roughly proportional to seq_len^2 for dense attention. If we keep model context to N_local + N_cache where N_cache uses cached KV (O(N_local * d) each step), incremental per-token cost dominated by N_local. So aim to push as much state as KV as possible to avoid quadratic blowup.
- Example: if N_local=512 and full context=4096, naive attention cost ~ (4096^2) vs cached approach cost ~ (512^2 + 512*4096) — huge savings with correct KV handling.

Experiment ideas (priority order):
1) Micro-bench KV cache serialization formats: FP16 vs int8 vs custom quantized. Measure memory, decode latency, and quality drift on multi-turn dialogue. Track metrics: perplexity on held convo steps, regeneration mismatch rate.
2) Eviction policy A/B: LRU vs attention-mass: instrument attention scores to create salience signal; evaluate user-visible regressions.
3) Retrieval + local cache hybrid: when retrieval returns docs, push their salient spans into KV (ephemeral) for the current convo; test for reduced grounding errors.
4) Adaptive local window that expands on low-latency budget: small default window (256), expand to 1024 when user signals (e.g., long-context queries).

Quick heuristics (for product conversations):
- Keep last-turn tokens + 2x important-turn tokens in KV for responsiveness.
- Favor TTL-based evictions for ephemeral chats; favor permanence for user profile features (index externally instead).
- Disable heavy re-ranking on cold paths; do async full-context re-score if latency budget exceeded.

Open questions / research probes:
- How much quality is lost when aggressively quantizing KV vs quantizing model weights? (we assume KV quantization is more forgiving but needs experiments).
- Are there simple salience predictors we can run cheaply to prioritize what to cache? Could be small classifier on turn features.
- How to support multi-device clients (mobile + web) with consistent KV state without incurring sync storms? Possible solution: server-side primary with client hints.

Notes-to-self / references to follow up:
- Re-run experiment from PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/71, focus on int8 serialization speed. Samir to help with test harness.
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-1234 (design doc for adaptive eviction); add cost table and sample traces.
- Slack thread: #kv-cache-ops — summarize best current practices and paste example attention-salience plot.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Implement micro-benchmark harness for cache serialization (owner: Harper). Due: 2027-08-30.
- Quick survey notebook that loads three small models and reports memory/latency for FP16 vs int8 KV caches (owner: Samir). Due: 2027-08-25.
- Draft short internal note with recommended default: "ttl=30m, LRU fallback, quantized KV int8" and circulate to eng-sre and serving-runtime teams. (owner: Harper + Iris).

End of cheatsheet — keep this file short, copy items into more formal doc if pushing to product/console.

Misc raw links to read: 
- Local attention & chunking survey: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.06732
- KV cache paper we benchmarked earlier: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17580
- Example GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/71
